questions.stem: What is the name of the curve obtained when a plane cuts the nappe of a cone at an angle of 90 degrees?
questions.solution: When a plane cuts the nappe of a cone at a right angle, the resulting curve is a circle because the intersection forms a perfectly round shape. An ellipse is formed when the plane is tilted at an angle less than 90 degrees but not parallel to the side. A parabola occurs when the plane is parallel to the cone's side, and a hyperbola is created when the plane intersects both nappes of the cone.

questions.stem: What is the definition of the axis of a parabola?
choices: The line perpendicular to the directrix and passing through the focus.
The line that is equidistant from the focus and the directrix.
The line that intersects the parabola at two points.
The line that is parallel to the directrix and passes through the focus.
questions.solution: The axis of a parabola is the line that is perpendicular to the directrix and passes through the focus, as it serves as the line of symmetry for the parabola. The second option incorrectly describes a line equidistant from the focus and directrix, which is not the definition of the axis. The third option refers to a secant line, not the axis, and the fourth option is parallel to the directrix, which contradicts the definition of the axis.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the standard form of the equation of a hyperbola with its transverse axis along the x-axis?
questions.solution: The standard form of a hyperbola with its transverse axis along the x-axis is x²/a² - y²/b² = 1. The other forms represent ellipses or hyperbolas with the transverse axis along the y-axis.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a degenerated case of a hyperbola?
questions.solution: A hyperbola can degenerate into a pair of intersecting lines when the plane passes through the apex of the cone. A point is a degenerate ellipse, a straight line is a degenerate parabola, and a circle is not a degenerate conic section. Therefore, the correct answer is a pair of intersecting lines.

questions.stem: The equation of the ellipse with major axis along the x-axis and semi-major axis of length 'a' and semi-minor axis of length 'b' is given by which of the following?
questions.solution: The standard equation of an ellipse with the major axis along the x-axis is x²/a² + y²/b² = 1. This is directly derived from the geometric definition of an ellipse where the sum of distances from two foci is constant. The other options represent hyperbolas or incorrect orientations of the ellipse.

questions.stem: What is the center and radius of the circle given by the equation (x + 5) + (y – 3) = 36?
questions.solution: The equation (x + 5) + (y – 3) = 36 can be written as (x – (–5)) + (y – 3) = 6². Hence, the center is (–5, 3) and the radius is 6. The other options are incorrect due to errors in signs or misinterpreting the radius as the squared value.
